gaps.discriminates: Presence of hypoxia would support pneumonia severity and help distinguish from mild atelectasis or non-infectious pleuritis; absence of hypoxia makes severe pneumonia or PE less likely but does not exclude early bacterial pneumonia.

Positive blood culture would confirm bacteremia and strongly support invasive bacterial pneumonia over viral, aspiration-related, or non-infectious mimics (e.g., postoperative atelectasis with reactive inflammation).

Identification of typical bacterial pathogens (e.g., S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae) supports community-acquired or healthcare-associated bacterial pneumonia; absence of organisms or presence of atypical flora may suggest aspiration, viral, or non-infectious etiology.
